title: KV adaptive TTL autotuner and roll-forward playbook for safe cache config changes
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket defines an operational playbook and engineering changes to introduce an adaptive TTL autotuner for KV/prefix caches, a conservative key-shaping recommendation set, and a safe roll-forward mechanism to apply cache policy adjustments automatically while enabling near-instant rollback on regressions. Goal: reduce token spend by improving effective hit rate while protecting user-facing latency and output quality.
background: We currently rely on static TTLs and heuristic key shapes for prefix and KV caches. Prior work (ENG-4821, ENG-7934, ENG-12897) showed large variance in per-customer hit rates and cost benefits; manual tuning is slow and risk-prone. Teams want an automated way to propose TTL changes, validate them against workload simulations and live canaries, and apply them with minimal operational overhead. This playbook combines a hit-curve forecaster (hit probability vs. TTL), simulated cost delta, and a roll-forward process that uses metric gates to either commit or rollback changes.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a hit-curve estimator service that consumes sample traces and returns expected hit rate and marginal hit improvement for a TTL sweep per prefix family. 2) Implement an adaptive TTL autotuner that proposes per-prefix TTL candidates and a confidence score; integrate with Console to preview cost/latency projections. 3) Create a simulated apply harness that runs candidate policies against historical traces and synthetic batches to surface tail-latency and failure risk. 4) Deploy a roll-forward controller that performs staged canaries (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated metric gating and an immediate rollback path.
kv_key_design_recommendations: - Canonicalize keys to remove request-local UUIDs and timestamps; include only semantic tokens (user-id, model-id, prompt-fingerprint). - Prefer short prefix granularity for high-cardinality fields (e.g., user buckets) and coarse prefixes for shared prompts. - Use a stable hashing layer for non-sensitive identifiers to enable even distribution without exposing PII. - Append sequence-length bucket when KV entries vary strongly with context length to avoid polluting hot-key entries.
hit_rate_modeling: - Use exponentially-weighted recency windows to estimate per-prefix access frequency. - Construct hit curves by measuring unique-key lifetime distributions; produce a function H(TTL) that yields expected hit rate given TTL. - Include burst damping: detect and discount short-term spikes (traffic surges) so TTLs aren't overstretched. - Quantify uncertainty: report a 90% confidence interval for predicted hit uplift; prefer conservative picks when uncertainty is high.
ttl_policy_tuning: - Policy tiers: conservative, balanced, aggressive. Conservative requires >50% predicted uplift and <5% tail-latency change; balanced allows lower confidence with manual review; aggressive auto-applies only for non-critical namespaces. - Ramp candidates by multiplicative factors (1.5x, 2x) rather than absolute seconds for consistent effect across prefixes. - Minimum TTL floor and maximum cap enforced per prefix-family to avoid runaway growth.
simulation_and_validation_plan: - Create a trace playback harness that replays sampled requests against current cache policy and candidate policies to estimate hit, cost delta, and tail latency. - Run A/B offline simulations using historical traffic slices and synthetic cold-starts. - Validate output quality by sampling a small fraction of requests and re-running model inference without cache to detect divergent outputs; track semantic-quality regression via prompts/ground-truth evals.
rollforward_and_safe_apply: - Staged rollout: preview -> dry-run (no traffic) -> canary 1% (24h) -> canary 10% (24h) -> broad 50% (6h) -> full 100%. - Metric gates at each stage: token-cost delta, cache hit-rate delta, 95th/99th latency, model error rate, and QA-sampled semantic regression. - If any gate crosses threshold, controller immediately scales traffic back to previous stage and initiates automated rollback with an incident note. - All changes are stored as immutable policy versions with tombstone/undo metadata for single-click rollbacks in Console.
rollback_playbook: 1) Detect gate violation from rollforward controller. 2) Pause rollforward and route affected traffic to previous policy version. 3) Notify owners via Slack and create incident with automatic links to simulation artifacts and difference report. 4) If rollback is insufficient, migrate traffic to fallback model variant (lower-cost but higher-latency) or increase dedicated capacity temporarily. 5) Postmortem: record root cause, adjust hit-curve hyperparameters or key-shaping rules, and schedule follow-up tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner service produces per-prefix TTL proposals with confidence scores and simulated delta estimates
Simulation harness can replay traces and output cost/hit/latency comparisons for candidate policies
Rollforward controller implements staged canaries with automated metric gates and completes rollouts without manual intervention in >= 80% of test runs
Rollback playbook executes within 5 minutes from gate violation and reduces customer-facing error/latency back to baseline
Console displays proposed policy diffs, projected cost savings, and an audit trail for applied policy versions
metrics: per-prefix cache hit rate (baseline and post-change)
tokens served per model per minute
experiment_plan: 1) Select three non-critical namespaces with varied traffic shapes (chat, embeddings, reranking). 2) Run offline simulation for candidate TTL sweeps and choose conservative and balanced candidates. 3) Execute staged rollouts in staging environment, then in production canaries per rollout policy. 4) Collect and compare metrics; refine hit-curve parameters. 5) Expand to 20 namespaces over 6 weeks.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: autotuner overfits on bursty windows -> Mitigation: use burst damping and require multi-day signals. - Risk: semantic regressions due to changed KV eviction patterns -> Mitigation: sample outputs and maintain an eval suite that tracks quality for top prompts. - Risk: hot-key amplification -> Mitigation: detect hot-key clusters and apply per-key caps or shard keys.
notes: Keep default behavior unchanged for high-SLA namespaces unless explicit opt-in. Provide an escape hatch for customers to pin TTLs. Coordinate launch with Support and Solutions teams to handle customer inquiries about changed cache behavior.
